newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: IMF sees Germany, France missing EMU goal - paper.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Germany, France missing EMU goal - paper.

text.p: Both Germany and France will miss the single currency entry target of a budget deficit of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, a Portuguese newspaper quoted the International Monetary Fund's latest World Economic Outlook as saying.

Diario Economico, which said it had had access to the report, said the IMF predicted a German deficit of 3.3 percent in 1997 and 2.9 percent in 1998, while the figures for France were 3.3 and 3.4 percent respectively.
Italy's deficit was put at 3.3 percent in 1997 but it would then rise to 4.1 percent the following year.

Germany's debt-to-GDP ratio was also seen slightly exceeding the 60 percent guideline at 61.5 and 61.1 percent in the two years. Its economy was seen growing 2.3 percent in 1997 and three percent in 1998.

Portugal, however, was seen hitting its budget deficit target of 2.9 percent for this year, with the figure falling to 2.5 percent in 1998. Its inflation was forecast at 2.5 percent this year, easing to 2.3 percent in 1998.
